mode: actual X11 screen capture of a dedicated Kitty window; actual Neovim, Rust server, and Pi adapter
model: Pi faux provider with fixed responses; no provider credentials supplied
tools: actual Pi bash tool and Python syntax check in a temporary project
input: keys sent to the terminal with Kitty remote control
capture: FFmpeg x11grab restricted to the terminal window

steps.text: Run the launch script from the project directory.
Press ; in normal mode. Agents appear under project folders.
Press n. Enter a name to create an agent in this project.
Type a task in the prompt. Press Ctrl-S to send it.
The actual bash tool checks the file. The answer streams into the transcript.
Move back to the source window after the first task completes.
Return to the tree. Select another stored agent with Enter.
Start a second task. Use s on its tree row to stop only that agent.
Press ; to hide the tree. Use :qa to close after all tasks have stopped.
The demonstration is complete. All model text came from the Pi faux provider.

assertions: normal editor starts with one window
semicolon displays stored agents grouped by workspace
submitted task appears in the stored transcript
actual tool output contains Syntax check passed.
normal exit closes Neovim after work stops
cleanup: all demonstration sessions stopped; private server shut down; terminal closed
